A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FourierSHAP work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-F. v3 removes the NeurIPS checklist, but the research material remains complete and reliably matchable.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original Fourier approximation, SHAP accuracy, and runtime experiments involving neural networks and tree ensembles on four datasets.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds absolute runtime measurements and larger query/background-size experiments in Appendix E.1.2.

M1.justification: The sparse Fourier approximation, exact tree conversion, SHAP formula in Equation 5, and implementations in Appendix D are retained. Added intuition and the abstract's explicit binary-input qualification do not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Entacmaea, SGEMM, GB1, and avGFP with the same representations and tasks. The additional runtime experiments vary query/background sample counts within retained coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain KernelSHAP, LinRegSHAP, FastSHAP, DeepLift, TreeSHAP, GPU TreeSHAP, FastTreeSHAP, and PLTreeSHAP. The added runtime tests reuse KernelSHAP; existing comparisons do not gain or lose baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix E.1.2 adds a runtime experiment crossing query and background sizes of 100, 200, 300, and 400, beyond the retained black-box grid of 10, 20, 30, and 40. Existing training settings, accuracy metrics, and tree-evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New runtime tables examine how computation scales with query and background sizes, including substantially larger sets. This adds a limited scalability analysis; existing pruning tradeoffs, tree-depth comparisons, and KernelSHAP convergence checks are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions describe variation across 16 black-box query/background configurations and standard deviations over five independent tree runs. The new runtime tables introduce no additional run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or significance reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 1 reports SGEMM KernelSHAP runtimes of 2.0-17.9 seconds. New Table 2 reports larger-set timings, including 265 seconds for KernelSHAP versus 213 milliseconds for FourierSHAP at 400 queries and 400 background points. Figures 1-5 and the older training-time and convergence tables retain their results.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, propositions, Lemma 1, Theorem 2, and Appendix B proofs are unchanged. The added parity-cancellation paragraph explains existing reasoning without adding a formal result or proof step.

C1.justification: The abstract now explicitly qualifies the main applicability claim to binary-input predictors, a restriction previously stated in the body. The central claims about exact Fourier-based SHAP computation, amortization, speedups, and the accuracy-efficiency tradeoff remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix E.1.2 newly explains that slow KernelSHAP and LinRegSHAP computations motivated the small background sets, and interprets the added absolute timings as evidence of practical benefits. The continuous-feature and conditional-SHAP limitations in Appendix F are retained.

D1.justification: v2 promises public code release after review; v3 states that the code is publicly available and supplies a project repository address. Hardware, implementation variants, hyperparameters, and preprocessing information are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds Huang et al. (2024) and Marzouk et al. (2024, 2025), briefly extending the discussion of observational-SHAP computational complexity. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized prose revisions, adds intuition after Lemma 1, moves the discretization explanation from a footnote into the body, and adds a limitations cross-reference and acknowledgments. It removes the administrative checklist while retaining the research section structure.

P2.justification: v3 adds two runtime tables, with Table 2 divided into KernelSHAP and FourierSHAP panels. Existing figure graphics and table contents are retained; Figure 3 moves after the conclusion, and the older tables are renumbered amid local layout changes.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the relative-speedup claims easier to assess through absolute runtimes and larger-size tests in Tables 1-2. It also clarifies the binary-input scope in the abstract, explains Lemma 1, and provides concrete code-access information. These improve clarity, practical evidence, and reproducibility documentation, while the method, proofs, and benchmark coverage remain unchanged.
